news.title: Senate Rewards Flamingos With N100m for FIFA U-17 World Cup Triumph
news.lede: The Nigerian Senate has announced a cash reward of N100 million for the U-17 women’s national football team, the Flamingos, following their historic victory at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Rabat, Morocco. The pledge followed a motion moved by the Chairman of the Senate Committee on Sports, Senator Abdul Ningi, who congratulated the players for their outstanding performance and commended the Nigeria Football Federation for its role in the team’s historic feat. The Flamingos made history by becoming the first African team to win the tournament after defeating Japan 2-1 in Saturday’s final. The Senate also commended President Bola Ahmed Tinubu for the team’s achievement, as well as his administration’s support for sports development and funding in the country.

news.title: Happening: Senate proposes financial reward for Nigeria 's Flamingos days after U-17 World Cup triumph
news.lede: November 10, 2026 Austine Agbo Emmanuel Sports, Top Stories 0. The Nigerian Senate is planning to reward the country’s victorious Under-17 women’s national football team, the Flamingos, following their historic triumph at the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco. The motion was moved on Tuesday during plenary by the Chairman of the Senate Committee on Sports, Senator Abdul Ahmed Ningi, who represents Bauchi Central Senatorial District of Bauchi state, blueprint reports. Senator Ningi proposed N100 million as reward from the Red Chamber for the Flamingos.

news.title: U-17 Women’s World Cup: Senate donates N100m to Flamingos
news.lede: Flamingos after World Cup triumph against Japan. The Senate has announced a donation of N100 million to Nigeria’s Under-17 women’s national football team, the Flamingos, following their historic victory at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Rabat, Morocco. The Senate President, Godswill Akpabio, announced the donation during plenary on Tuesday while presiding over a motion moved by Sen. Abdul Ningi (ADC-Bauchi Central) on the need to congratulate the victorious girls on their achievement.

news.title: "Seasoned internationals with younger players": Ellis names Banyana squad
news.lede: PAY ATTENTION: Mark Briefly News as a preferred source, and our content will appear higher in your Google feed! Coach Desiree Ellis has named her final 23-player Banyana Banyana squad ahead of South Africa's FIFA Women's World Cup preliminary play-offs in Rabat, Morocco. The team's target is a place at the 2027 World Cup in Brazil. The tournament runs from 28 November to 5 December 2026 at the Mohammed VI Football Complex, and South Africa must finish in the top two to advance to the final qualification phase scheduled for February 2027.

news.title: Nwifuru celebrates Flamingos’ historic World Cup victory, urges more investment in women’s football
news.lede: Ebonyi State Governor, Francis Nwifuru, has congratulated Nigeria’s Under-17 women’s national football team, the Flamingos, on their historic 2-1 victory over Japan to win the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco. The Governor on Tuesday in Abakaliki described the triumph as a landmark achievement in Nigeria’s sporting history, noting that the Flamingos had made the country proud by becoming the first African nation to win the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. Nigeria secured the historic victory on Saturday, November 7, 2026, following goals from Awawu Bashiru in the 39th minute and Oluebube Umejiaku in the 47th minute, while Japan’s Fuki Ito scored a late goal in the 80th minute.
